passage:
I'm Reena, and I still remember how my chest dropped when Sir said, in front of the class, "This doesn't sound like you." I had written that essay over three evenings, and asked a chatbot only twice for a better word than "sad".
My first instinct was to snap. Yusuf, at the next desk, whispered, "Show him your notebook."
So after class I stayed, hands shaking, and laid out my rough drafts, my scribbled notes and the two word suggestions. "I used it for two words," I said. "The rest is mine."
Sir looked through the pages slowly. Then he said, "Thank you for telling me." I have never hidden help since.

qa.q: How many times did Reena ask the chatbot for a better word than "sad"?
What was Reena feeling when the teacher said the essay didn't sound like Reena, and how do you know?
qa.a: Reena's chest dropped, the hands shook and there was an urge to snap, which suggests hurt, fear of not being believed, and anger. 😔

qa.q: What did Reena do that helped?
qa.a: Reena stayed calmly after class, showed the rough drafts, notes and word suggestions, and said honestly what help had been used.

qa.q: How might the teacher have seen the essay before Reena showed the notebook?
qa.a: The teacher may have noticed a style unlike Reena's usual writing and worried about honesty, and then valued Reena's openness.

grounding: Shows a student calmly showing drafts and notes and honestly naming a small use of AI when a teacher suspected the work.

passage:
In the government school in Barabanki, Asif sir held up Farhan's essay on the village pond. "This is too good, Farhan. Did the computer write it?"

The whole class turned. Farhan's face burned. He had spent two evenings on it at the tea stall, under the bulb, while his father served customers.

He wanted to shout. Instead he took a breath. "No, sir. I wrote it. Can I show you?"

After class he opened his rough notebook: crossed-out lines, a sketch of the pond, a first draft with spelling mistakes. "This is from Tuesday. This from Wednesday."

Asif sir turned the pages slowly.

"One more thing, sir," Farhan said. "My cousin's phone has a chatbot app. I asked it for three words that mean 'dirty.' I used 'murky' from it. That's all."

Asif sir looked at him for a long moment. Then he nodded. "Thank you for telling me that. I'm sorry I said it in front of everyone." He returned the essay with a mark and a small tick beside "murky."

qa.q: Where did Farhan write the essay?
qa.a: Farhan wrote it at the tea stall, under the bulb, while his father served customers.

qa.q: What was Farhan feeling when Asif sir questioned him in front of the class?
qa.a: Farhan felt humiliated and angry, with a burning face, and wanted to shout.

qa.q: What did Farhan do that was wise?
qa.a: Farhan stayed calm, showed his dated drafts and sketches, and honestly admitted using the app for one word.

qa.q: How does Asif sir seem to feel after seeing the notebook?
qa.a: Asif sir seems convinced and a little regretful, apologising for accusing Farhan in front of everyone.

grounding: It shows a teen suspected by a teacher of using AI for work that was mostly his own, calmly showing drafts and being honest about the small help he used.
